corpus_forum/cf_13405_forum_formation_ch: Chapter Thirteen names the forum families; **CF-13.405** is where an adopting entity turns those names into working benches, chambers, and support structures. It sets the minimum each family must actually staff and run, keeps families from quietly collapsing into one another, and states what a chamber may and may not decide.
corpus_forum/cf_13410_panel_formation_di: **CF-13.410** decides who is allowed to sit on a case. It states what makes a panel lawful and independent, what must be disclosed before anyone touches the merits, when a member must step aside, and what happens when no independent panel can be formed at all.
corpus_forum/cf_13415_routing_operations: **CF-13.415** is day-to-day traffic control for cases — how a matter is classified on arrival, who triages it, when it may be transferred, and how anyone acting on another's behalf must be treated. Routing must be published and reviewable, so a case cannot be steered to a friendly venue in silence.
corpus_forum/cf_13420_appeal_secondary_r: **CF-13.420** makes sure a first decision is not automatically the last word. It sets the minimum review routes every forum family must keep open, labels what each disposition actually decided, and stops "you have not exhausted your options" from being used to run out the clock.
corpus_forum/cf_13425_integrity_safeguar: **CF-13.425** stops a body from judging its own conduct, and stops an interested party from quietly capturing the body that reviews it. It covers alignment rulings, when a matter must be routed away from a compromised venue, and what happens when a whole forum family is compromised rather than a single member.
corpus_forum/cf_13430_forum_forensic_ana: **CF-13.430** gives a forum access to qualified technical help when the facts are too specialized, hidden, or tangled to weigh unaided. That help explains the evidence; it does not decide the case, prosecute it, or become a second forum.
corpus_forum/cf_13435_independent_invest: **CF-13.435** requires investigators independent enough to follow the facts wherever they lead, and keeps investigating a matter separate from deciding to charge, sanction, or close it. No body may investigate itself.
corpus_forum/cf_13440_technical_speciali: **CF-13.440** lets a system use scientific, engineering, and medical expertise without letting that expertise harden into an unaccountable parallel judiciary. Specialist bodies sit inside the Chapter Thirteen families, publish the standards they apply, and stay reviewable.
corpus_forum/cf_13445_performance_backlo: **CF-13.445** treats delay and inaccessibility as constitutional failures rather than administrative inconvenience. A forum that formally exists but is too slow, too opaque, or too hard to use is not doing its job, so this file sets what must be measured, the thresholds that trigger alarm, and the fixes required once one is crossed.
corpus_forum/cf_13450_forum_continuity.m: **CF-13.450** states what forums must keep doing when normal operation breaks down — emergency conditions, missing key staff, no lawful panel available, or infrastructure failure. Procedure may be simplified; the right to contest a decision may not be erased.
corpus_forum/cf_13455_fallback_operation: **CF-13.455** is the temporary substitute for a forum that cannot sit — a reduced quorum, a backup venue, or a transfer away from a compromised family. It is temporary by design: it must record what it did and hand the matter back.
corpus_forum/cf_13460_emergency_adjudica: **CF-13.460** governs how urgent matters are decided while ordinary operation is degraded — what gets priority, who reviews emergency decisions while they are still in force, and how everything is reconciled once normal operation returns. An emergency is not a licence to decide without record or review.
corpus_forum/cf_13465_standard_records_f: **CF-13.465** is the paperwork floor. It gathers the record duties scattered across **CF-13.410** through **CF-13.460** into one minimum set — what must be captured, which fields it must carry, who may see it, and how long it is kept — so a decision can still be checked long after it was made.
corpus_forum/cf_13470_staffing_reserve_c: **CF-13.470** covers whether a forum has enough qualified staff to function at all — how competence is defined, how support staff advance into adjudicative roles, what reserve capacity exists for surges, and which structural records prove it. Shared administration must not become a back door for steering cases.
